title: Sub-agent
description: ADR-0013: a host-declared reads-only child. The host pins pinnedDigest at approval; the package computes digest over canonical JSON of all definition members except pinnedDigest and digest. Tools are declared host wire names; skills are declared ids. Bounds only narrow the turn. Built-in profile ids cannot be declared. No nesting or child critic.

source.description: Where a host tool comes from (ADR-0006). Declared by the host on each host tool a source outside the host serves; the package adds tool (the tool's own name at its source) on the offer, carries the record on the tool's tool_call and tool_result events (with receipt on a result where the host's answer gave one), and counts the source in the run report (provenance.json#/$defs/sourceFigures). gateway: a gateway connection the person configured (Databricks, Azure DevOps, Drive), which may give a receipt for each call; mcp: a public MCP server the host connected, whose tool list is pinned by digest at connection time; custom: a tool the person created; exchange (ADR-0009): a skill whose bytes the host fetched from a Judgment Exchange entry, the entry's id and version the record's id and version, which a host tool may not declare. runtime is the Runtime's own row in the run report: its tools come through tools/list behind the gate, carry no declaration, and a host tool declared with kind runtime is refused. Either version or toolListDigest is present; mcp carries toolListDigest. Closed: the package refuses another member before any request (configuration).

id.description: The source's name as the host names it (a connection, a server, the person's own tools): a letter, then letters, digits and hyphens, at most 24 characters. Every wire name of the source's tools begins with it.

version.description: The source's version as the host knows it: a connection's revision, a server's version, a custom tool's revision.

trust.description: The trust class the host gives the source: first-party (the Runtime, and a source the host itself runs), connected (a connection the person configured with their own grants), public (a public server), person (a tool the person wrote). Reported, never a grant: whatever the class, the source's descriptions are untrusted text and its results data, and its tools are held to their effect class.
